coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: No Malian text found on declaring domestic staff. One business guide says INPS covers domestic employees 'to be verified'. Employer must report hires and dismissals to INPS within 8 days (CLEISS) and pay contributions by the 15th of the following month. Guides contradict each other on rates. Weak, low-income buyers; nothing new beyond K02 (payroll add-on).

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: Nothing Malian found. Only Niger (arrêté of 21 Nov 2024 banning scrap export) and Algeria turned up. No Malian licensing or register rule confirmed; unverified.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: No search spent (budget). No evidence either way.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: Decree 02-536 (2002) and interministerial arrêté 03-0239 (2003) set three categories: collecteurs (3-year professional card, stamped register of purchases and sales, semi-annual quantity report to DNGM), comptoirs d'achat et d'exportation (licence by Commerce minister) and exporters of gold jewellery. This is the same buyer group and duty as K03. Texts are old; I did not check whether the 2023 mining code replaced them.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: No search spent (budget).

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: No recent Malian text on declarations, laissez-passer or market fees. OECD notes informal border levies of about 75,000 FCFA. Cattle export to Côte d'Ivoire was re-authorised in 2026. Nothing new beyond K07, which concerns per-shipment certificates.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: Interministerial arrêté 2017-2298 governs sanitary inspection of animals and meat: ante-mortem inspection at least 24 hours before slaughter, slaughter only in approved abattoirs in towns that have one, inspection fees. State vets do the inspection. No butcher register or recurring report found. Weak.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: No search spent (budget).

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: Law 01-062 of 4 July 2001 and decree 01-34 of 9 Aug 2001 on veterinary pharmacy. Mandat sanitaire under arrêtés 96-1367 and 97-1559. A 2010 Ordre des vétérinaires presentation counts about 14 wholesalers, 30 branches and 500 practices, and flags counterfeit drugs. No recurring report to the authority confirmed. Weak candidate.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: The search returned only French and Moroccan material. The Water Code (loi 02-006 of 31 Jan 2002) exists, but I could not confirm any driller agrément or abstraction declaration. Unverified.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: Only old Eawag and academic studies (about 40,000 households use manual emptiers, 33,000 use trucks; GIE Sema Saniya in Bamako). No emptier licensing regime found. Weak.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: Only French material returned. No Malian periodic-inspection rule found. Not confirmed; low priority.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Water Code 2002 allows delegated management (affermage, gérance, régie intéressée) of water systems. In rural areas management goes mostly to user associations. Urban areas are served by SOMAGEP-SA under the electricity and water regulator CREE. No small-operator reporting duty or software gap confirmed.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: A Malian order requires a resale agrément (50,000 FCFA, 5 years renewable, minister's approval after national committee advice, locked store, annual staff medical exams, only registered products). A 2019 survey found 26% of pesticides sold unregistered. No applicator licence found. Small candidate, no clear recurring filing.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: Mali has the ANPE (since 2001) and private paid placement offices, but no private-agency licensing or reporting text was found. Unverified.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: Nothing Malian found; results were French, Belgian and Swiss. Not confirmed.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: Decree 2026-0152/PT-RM of 13 Mar 2026 and ministerial decision 2026-000223/MATD-SG of 7 May 2026 impose a 10% levy on development funds, a no-objection opinion for any grant, quarterly expenditure tables and activity reports, and prior notice of activities. In 2024 the council of ministers adopted a draft ordinance to amend the 2004 association law (loi 04-038) and make authorisation mandatory; adoption is unconfirmed. Strong new lead. Halal/kosher: nothing found.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: National registration campaign for two- and three-wheelers from 15 June 2026 under arrêté 2023-5150/MTI-SG: 12,000 FCFA per vehicle paid via TRESOR PAY, certificate valid 5 years, red plates for moto-taxis. Bamako digital municipal tax collection (K'lis pay) exists. Taxi-union online taxi project. No taxi, SOTRAMA or visite technique rules found.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Manual exchange agents fall under UEMOA Regulation 09/2010/CM/UEMOA and BCEAO Instruction 07/07/2025/RFE (in force 1 Aug 2025, regional). It requires a monthly report of all operations, and individual holders must re-apply as a legal entity within a year. The source was Benin's treasury, so the Malian transposition is unverified. Market fees and RCCM: nothing specific; the Bamako digital tax collection is a state tool.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Driving schools, nurseries and childminders: no Malian text found. Tattoo studios, small food producers and hunting outfitters: no search spent.

coverage.category: 21. Fuel stations and fuel or LPG distributors
coverage.found: Arrêté interministériel signed in Bamako on 30 Oct 2025 (press reports via APA News only, text not seen): stations open 24/7 until further notice; distributors must report stocks weekly to the Ministry of Commerce (quantities received and sold per fuel type); no sale in jerrycans without proof of professional or domestic use. 21 Nov 2025 protocol with importers to cut tanker declaration delay at the petroleum products office to one day. NDC Energie took over about 80 former TotalEnergies stations (Jan 2026). Reporting format, platform and sanctions not found. See candidate on weekly fuel-stock reporting.

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: Cereal export suspension since 6 Dec 2021 (FAO GIEWS); no 2025-2026 Malian text requiring grain traders to declare stocks. Shea kernel, groundnut, soy and sesame exports suspended by interministerial arrêté of 3 Oct 2024 (press); that is a ban, not a recurring filing. Nothing new beyond bans; no recurring workflow found.

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: Decentralised financial systems (SFD) must send annual reports, audited financial statements and quarterly statistics to the supervision cell (CCS/SFD, Ministry of Finance); a control review flagged late filings and 6 mutualist networks reporting on 56 unlicensed base caisses (sources about 2006-2007, current regime unverified). Co-operative law 2001-076 plus OHADA co-operative uniform act (regional, 2010); co-operatives sit in a co-operative register run by the administration, not the RCCM; the holding authority in Mali was not confirmed. Tontines are outside the SFD regime. See SFD and co-operative candidates.

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes
coverage.found: AMO started in 2009, run by CANAM; 2011 agreements cover public hospitals and community health centres; no source on private clinic or lab accreditation, tariffs or third-party payment rules. A new AMO-covered medicines list for private pharmacies was validated in Jan 2020. No Malian private-clinic billing rule found; unverified rather than rejected.

coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals or precursors
coverage.found: Order of Pharmacists created by loi 2017-031 (14 Jul 2017), decree 2017-0722, deontology code 2017; DPM (pharmacy directorate) is the regulator. No source on the narcotics register or precursor reporting. AMO claims for private pharmacies exist (2020 list) but no detail on how they are filed or on existing pharmacy software.

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: Private guarding firms need an agrément from the Ministry of Security (example arrêté Dec 2006, published in the JO in 2008, preceded by a récépissé, revocable); a separate uniform rule exists. Current decree, ongoing registers and reporting duties not found. Unverified.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: Mining Code loi 2023-040 of 29 Aug 2023 (Title 10 on local content) and local-content loi 2023-041 of 29 Aug 2023; a 2026 decree on Kobada raises state and national participation to 35 percent; a national mining fund for subcontractors is only under discussion (capmad, Jul 2026). No subcontractor register, agrément or reporting procedure found: nothing new beyond K01.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: WAEMU uniform AML/CFT law covers non-financial professions (regional); CENTIF is the FIU. No Malian decree, thresholds or filing method for notaries or estate agents found; transposition status in Mali unverified. A Banque de France table (2017) showed half of the states had not transposed the uniform law. No gold-counter findings beyond K03 (not re-searched).

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: Only a dated travel-guide statement of a tourist tax of about 500 FCFA per person per night; no Malian text found on guest registers or police forms. Tourism demand is also depressed by the security situation. Unverified; weak.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: The EU suspended mango imports from Mali in 2025 after rising fruit-fly interceptions since 2022, and exporters shifted to Morocco and the UK (freshplaza, le360). Mango traceability rests on interministerial arrêté 06-287 of 14 Feb 2006 and EC reg. 178/2002, with an STDF-funded traceability kit (so donor-funded tooling exists). Export suspension for shea kernels, groundnuts, soy and sesame (3 Oct 2024). Exporters must be in the RCCM with tax ID and licence. Exporter agrément and phytosanitary procedure not confirmed.

coverage.category: 31. Mobile-money agents and sub-agents (WAEMU e-money rules)
coverage.found: E-money issuers are licensed by BCEAO under instruction 008-05-2015 (regional); BCEAO ordered Orange Money Mali to stop cross-border transfers in Feb 2017. Sub-agent duties and KYC reporting not found; the issuers' own apps probably dominate. Unverified.

coverage.category: 32. SIM-card identification (resellers and subscribers)
coverage.found: Decree 2015-0265/P-RM requires subscribers to link each number to a NINA; limit of 3 SIMs per subscriber and operator (2019 amendment); identification deadline moved from 15 Dec 2024 to 15 Apr 2025 (AMRTP). The deadline has passed and the burden falls on telcos and subscribers. No reseller duty found. Weak.

coverage.category: 33. Vehicle and two/three-wheeler registration
coverage.found: Mass registration of unregistered motorised two- and three-wheelers began 15 Jun 2026 (Ministry of Transport, announced 11 Jun 2026, nationwide); the government also stated that unregistered vehicles may not circulate since 30 Jun 2026 (seneweb). Registration rules in arrêté 2023-5150/MTI-SG of 29 Dec 2023. Done at state offices; fees, penalties and volumes not found. One-off, state-run; weak.

coverage.category: 34. Customs brokers (commissionnaires en douane agréés) and small declarants
coverage.found: Brokers are approved by the Ministry of Economy and Finance on the advice of the Customs Directorate; broker use is mandatory under the WTO facilitation workstream (UNCTAD slide); SYDONIA++ is the customs system (UNCTAD). Burkina results excluded. Current Malian conditions unverified.

coverage.category: 35. Microfinance/SFD supervision filings
coverage.found: See category 23. Regime of agrément or convention under the WAEMU SFD law, CCS/SFD supervision, periodic reports. Candidate below.

coverage.category: 36. Foreign-trade formalities platform (SYGOCE, May 2025) and trade-licence requirements
coverage.found: One search summary tied SYGOCE to four digital platforms presented in May 2025, but a follow-up search found no source naming SYGOCE; unverified. A CCIM-led consultation on simplifying foreign-trade formalities is under way (apanews). Operators must hold an RCCM entry, tax ID and a valid patente. Nothing actionable.

coverage.category: 37. Private schools and private health establishments (opening authorisation and census)
coverage.found: Nothing found on private-school or private-clinic authorisation criteria or a census. Context: 2,444 schools did not reopen on 1 Oct 2026 (about 733,000 children), caused by insecurity. Not applicable as a lead from this search.

candidates.name: Motorcycle (125 cc and above) dealer stock declaration and import-suspension compliance
candidates.trigger: Interministerial arrêté of 3 June 2026 (signed by the ministers of Defence, Justice, Territorial Administration, Security and Transport): import, transit, sale and distribution of motorcycles of 125 cc and above and their accessories suspended for one year, renewable. Holders of stocks or orders in progress must declare them within 90 days or face seizure. That window ended around 1 September 2026.
candidates.unchecked: The official text and the renewal outcome (due about June 2027); whether spare parts count as 'accessoires'; how many dealers there are; any recurring reporting after the declaration. No competitor search was run (score under 3).

candidates.name: Assisted registration service for owners of two- and three-wheelers (motorcycles, tricycles, moto-taxis)
candidates.trigger: National registration operation for two- and three-wheelers launched 15 June 2026 by the Ministry of Transport, run by the Direction générale des Transports, its regional offices and dedicated centres. The legal basis is the arrêté of 29 December 2023 (registration number and certificate valid 5 years). A Senegalese outlet reports a ban on unregistered vehicles from 30 June 2026 with 12 months to regularise; single secondary source, unverified. No deadline or fine amount found.
candidates.unchecked: The deadline, fees, penalties, and whether registration is online or in person. Whether buyers are individuals (out of scope) or fleet and moto-taxi operators (in scope). Competitor search not run for lack of budget; no local-language search for 'assistance immatriculation moto Mali' was possible. One-off, with weak willingness to pay and a security-driven, unstable regime.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: Five searches in French and English (friperie, brocante, gage, recel, police register, pawn lending). No Malian text found that creates a licence or a police or transaction register for second-hand dealers, friperie traders or pawnbrokers. Search results were French, Quebec, Singapore, South African and Australian regimes only, none applicable. Friperie is a large, mostly informal women-led trade (Afrik.com, undated) with no Mali-specific rule found. Pawn lending: no source classes it as a regulated activity. Only context found is the 2025 microfinance law reform (116 licensed SFDs at end-2024, drive against unlicensed lenders, APA News), which could in theory catch unlicensed pawn-style lenders; unverified. No candidate. Not checked: Code pénal recel text, communal patente rules, the Journal officiel.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: Six searches and three fetches. No Malian rule found on dismantlers, end-of-life vehicles, or a used-parts register or provenance duty. Bamako's fleet is mostly imported used cars (Le360, 19 May 2024: sources now Belgium, US, Benin, Korea; no age limit or parts mention). Only official hook found: WTO-notified arrêté 2015-1535/MCI/MEF-SG of 5 June 2015 requiring transport-ministry authorisation for vehicles above 3.5 t. A commercial site claims a 10-year age cap; unverified. The new motorcycle measures of June 2026 are the only fresh rules touching vehicle traders: the interministerial arrêté of 3 June 2026 suspends import and sale of motorcycles of 125 cc and above and their accessories for one renewable year, with a 90-day stock declaration, and registration of all two- and three-wheelers began on 15 June 2026. These are logged as weak candidates. A faolex PDF (mli158685) could not be read (scanned image). Not checked: the text of the 2015 arrêté, whether 'accessoires' includes spare parts.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: Four searches and one fetch. No Malian beekeeping regulator, register, licence, certification scheme or association was found. Honey exports are negligible (Trading Economics, UN COMTRADE: about US$5.1k to the US in 2023, about US$1.7k to Gambia in 2022). The only Mali source is a Le360 profile (6 May 2026) of one Bamako beekeeper producing 4 to 5 tonnes a year, formalised around 2011, which names no association, rule or export channel. No recurring mandatory duty found. No candidate. Not checked: ministry or ANSSA honey-safety rules, any bio/export certification body, the Chambre d'agriculture.

result.competitor: I found no Mali-specific tool for the decree's quarterly tables, activity reports or levy. I saw no state e-portal mentioned. Generic NGO project and grant tools exist for francophone Africa: Kolonell sells grant and M&E software and writes about Kinshasa, Cotonou and Antananarivo. International platforms such as ActivityInfo and DevResults are also used, as are KoboToolbox plus spreadsheets and SYCEBNL accounting. None is tailored to MATD templates or 10% levy tracking. The competitor search was limited to one query.
result.duty: Real and in force. Decree 2026-0152/PT-RM (13 Mar 2026) and its implementing MATD-SG decision (7 May 2026) apply to the following groups. Ordinary associations that receive aid. Associations with a framework agreement (accord-cadre). Public-utility associations. Foreign associations. National and foreign foundations. Any association that receives state, local-authority or donor funding. Obligations: 1) quarterly tables of spending, with the source of funds; 2) quarterly activity reports on a ministry template; 3) for each activity, purchase receipts and reception reports certified by the State representative, who must be told before the activity takes place; 4) prior no-objection from the minister (Art. 7) for each grant; 5) a 10% levy on development resources, which must be written into budgets and action plans. Hivos says the levy took 'immediate effect'. Sanctions run from formal notice to suspension, withdrawal of the récépissé or framework agreement, or a total ban, with no judicial appeal. Exempt: associations using only their own funds, projects that had a no-objection before the decree took effect, and humanitarian aid in crises. Not found: how the levy is collected, a clear entry-into-force date, the template text, and any e-portal.
result.market: Not reached. I found no current count of registered associations or accord-cadre NGOs in Mali. An EU roadmap cites accord-cadre statistics, but the figures were not visible. Likely a few thousand donor-funded associations and NGOs, but this is unverified. The market is shrinking: NGOs fear donor withdrawal, and NGOs with French funding were banned in 2022.
result.reason: The duty is real and recurring: quarterly reports and expenditure tables, a per-grant no-objection, the 10% levy, and harsh sanctions with no appeal. No tailored tool was seen. But several things cut against it. The buyers' budgets are being squeezed by the levy itself. Donors may pull out, and the hostile political climate makes the segment unstable. The ministry template is unpublished and so is the levy mechanism, which makes an MVP hard to specify. Funded NGOs often already use donor-imposed tools or accountants. Many local associations are very small and pay little. Also unknown: how many organisations there are, and whether MATD will build its own portal. A done-for-you compliance service run with accountants in Bamako is more plausible than SaaS.

The duty is real. The Ministry of Transport campaign (communiqué n°02-MTI-2026) began on 15 June 2026. It covers all unregistered motorcycles and tricycles, costs 12,000 FCFA per vehicle via TRESOR PAY, and requires ID, a residence certificate and proof of ownership. The certificate is valid for 5 years, under arrêté 2023-5150/MTI-SG. I found no end date or extension. One Seneweb snippet mentions a 12-month grace period for plateless vehicles, but it is unclear whether it covers motorcycles. I found no private software or online assisted service, but the job is in-person paperwork at state offices. Weaknesses: one-off, cash-based, low-income owners, thin margins, informal fixers likely, no recurring workflow, and the 125cc import ban shrinks the market. I did not find a market count. Not run: municipal tax and professional card checks.

The duty looks real but was only partly checked. UEMOA Regulation 09/2010 and BCEAO Instruction 07/07/2025/RFE (in force 1 Aug 2025) govern manual exchange agents. Individuals must convert to legal entities within one year. A guide from Côte d'Ivoire says agents prepare a detailed monthly report of all transactions. Instruction 15/07/2025/RFE sends periodic reports to the external-finance structure and the BCEAO. I could not read its Annex 2, so the monthly format, recipient and Mali application are unconfirmed. No Mali register or agent count was found. Benin had 106 agents, so Mali is probably a few dozen at most. No dedicated software was found, but my searches were thin. The market is tiny and regional, and the buyers are hard to reach, so I score it 3.

CLEISS says employers must notify INPS of hires and dismissals within 8 days. A commercial guide says INPS covers domestic workers, but it flags that as "to verify". I found no official text confirming household employers must declare domestic staff. Penalty figures (1.5% a month) come from one secondary guide only. I found no INPS online portal or app for household employers, so competition is probably thin. Informal employment is likely widespread, so few households would comply or pay. The market size is unknown, with no register or statistic found. Pain is low, willingness to pay is low, and buyers are hard to reach. I ran two searches and no fetches, so I didn't read the Labour Code or INPS texts directly.

APA reports an interministerial arrêté signed 30 Oct 2025 requiring weekly stock reporting to the Commerce ministry (quantities received and sold per fuel), 24/7 opening, and a jerrycan ban. I found no official text, arrêté number, penalty, report format or channel. I could not confirm it is still in force in Oct 2026; later articles mention only weekly arrival monitoring. The state is also building its own digital pump-rationing tool (DGCC, Jan 2026, per Digital Business Africa), which would overlap with or replace private reporting. The rule is crisis-driven and may lapse. No private software competitor found, but no market count either. Weak, uncertain duty, so the score stays low.

Duty is real: Loi 10-013 of 20 May 2010 (decree 10-315), amended in 2019 (loi 2019-032, art. 6), governs SFDs. The BCEAO monographs show about 125 approved SFDs in 2010-2011, but only 36 to 43 filed financial statements, so late or non-filing is common. I could not open the law text, so I could not confirm the exact filing frequency, the penalties, or the CCS/SFD templates. Competition is partial: Sibanque and Microbanker (2001 guide), plus local vendor kolonell.com, which sells Bamako SFD software with BCEAO reporting at 25 to 90 million FCFA. Buyers are tiny and poor, and Mali's insecurity weakens willingness to pay. The count of small independent SFDs is unclear. Competitor search was shallow.
